notes.author: user
notes.text: Monitor memory occupied by each managed Next.js development server.

problem: The controller reports process state but not the memory cost of a Next.js development server. Operators cannot see which managed project is responsible for host pressure or verify whether a concurrency limit is sufficient.
scope: Measure aggregate resident memory for the complete controller-owned process tree, not only the package-manager parent PID, while the server is starting or running.
Expose current and peak RSS, sample age, and unavailable/unsupported state in the dashboard and read-only MCP status without continuously retaining an unbounded time series.
Use a bounded low-frequency sampler that stops with the process and has negligible idle cost; support Linux first and define a tested macOS adapter or an explicit unavailable state.
Add configurable warning thresholds as a follow-up-friendly service boundary, but do not automatically terminate a server in the first version.
title: Monitor memory used by managed server process trees
validation: Start a Next.js dev server with worker children and verify reported RSS approximates the sum of the owned process tree rather than only the root PID.
Verify current and peak values disappear or become explicitly stale after stop and sampling resources are released.
Verify monitoring adds negligible CPU and memory overhead with several projects and does no work for stopped projects.
Verify unsupported platform or permission failures degrade to an unavailable state without changing server lifecycle.
value: Humans and agents can identify expensive development servers and tune concurrency from measured host impact rather than guesswork.
